add_meta_titles_and_robots_per_route.s:
Exhaustive per-route pass, wiring [[add_public_site_url_and_seo_head_component]]'s `SeoHead` (and, for dynamic pages, per-instance title/description) into every route, with an explicit index/noindex decision for each — getting this wrong in either direction is a real SEO cost: indexing authenticated app shell wastes crawl budget and can surface thin/duplicate/user-specific content in search results; noindexing something that should be public (like a room page, now publicly viewable per [[wire_lazy_account_creation_into_room_join_and_send]] in the other plan) throws away free organic traffic to exactly the content this whole reorientation is built to surface.

Route-by-route decision table (index it if and only if a logged-out visitor can usefully land on it and it has unique, non-duplicate content):

| Route | Index? | Title pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | yes | static, set in [[add_public_site_url_and_seo_head_component]] |
| `/login` | no | "log in" |
| `/app/rooms` | yes (publicly viewable per the device-account plan) | "rooms" |
| `/app/rooms/[id]` | yes, dynamic | `{room name} — a room on x2` |
| `/app/user/[id]` | **no** — a private profile page, not a public directory entry; indexing individual user pages would leak usernames/interests into search results, which nothing in this product's design intends | n/a, still needs a title for the tab/bookmark, just noindexed |
| `/app/chat/[id]`, `/app/chats`, `/app/profile`, `/app` (people-matching) | no — all require a real session and show user-specific content | short static titles, all noindexed |
| `/blog`, `/blog/[slug]` | yes | handled in [[add_blog_routes]] |
| `/alternatives/*` | yes | handled in [[add_alternative_landing_pages]] |

Apply `<SeoHead>` to each currently-headless route:

`src/routes/login/+page.svelte` (read this file first to confirm it doesn't already have a `data`/load pattern to hook into) — add near the top of its markup:
```svelte
<SeoHead title="log in" description="log in to x2 to keep your rooms and messages across devices." path="{PUBLIC_SITE_URL}/login" noindex />
```
(needs `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` passed down from a `+page.server.ts` — add one if this route doesn't have one yet, mirroring the home page's pattern from [[add_public_site_url_and_seo_head_component]].)

`src/routes/app/rooms/+page.svelte`:
```svelte
<SeoHead title="rooms" description="search rooms built around what you're into, or start your own." path="{data.site_url}/app/rooms" />
```
(`data.site_url` — add to this route's existing `+page.server.ts` load return, same pattern.)

`src/routes/app/rooms/[id]/+page.svelte` — dynamic per-room title/description, and a room-specific JSON-LD block (schema.org has no perfect fit for "chat room"; `DiscussionForumPosting` or a generic `WebPage` with the room's description is the closest reasonable mapping — use `WebPage` to avoid overclaiming a schema type that doesn't quite match):
```svelte
<SeoHead
	title="{g.name} — a room on x2"
	description={g.description || `join ${g.name}, a room on x2 with ${g.members.length} members.`}
	path="{data.site_url}/app/rooms/{g.id}"
	jsonld={breadcrumb_jsonld([
		{ name: 'home', url: data.site_url },
		{ name: 'rooms', url: `${data.site_url}/app/rooms` },
		{ name: g.name, url: `${data.site_url}/app/rooms/${g.id}` }
	])}
/>
```
(add `import { breadcrumb_jsonld } from '$lib/seo';` and `import SeoHead from '$lib/components/SeoHead.svelte';`; `data.site_url` added to `+page.server.ts`'s existing return alongside `g`/`messages`/`names`/`muted`.)

Every other `/app/*` page not listed above gets a short static noindexed `<SeoHead>` call (title only needs to be human-useful for the browser tab/bookmark, description can be terse since it'll never surface in search):
- `/app/chats` → `title="chats"`
- `/app/profile` → `title="your profile"`
- `/app` (people-matching) → `title="match"` (matches the nav relabel from [[reorder_nav_rooms_first]]/[[rewrite_site_copy]] in the other plan)
- `/app/chat/[id]` → `title="chat"` (never include the peer's name in a noindexed page's title — no SEO benefit since it's noindexed anyway, and putting a second person's name in your own browser tab title is a minor, easily-avoided privacy leak via shoulder-surfing/screen-share)
- `/app/user/[id]` → `title="profile"`, explicitly `noindex`

Test: for each modified `.svelte` file, extend (or create) its component test with a `document.title`/meta-robots assertion matching the table above — e.g. for `/app/user/[id]`: `expect(document.querySelector('meta[name="robots"]')?.getAttribute('content')).toBe('noindex, nofollow');`, and for `/app/rooms/[id]`: title interpolates the actual room name. This is mechanical but exhaustive — one assertion pair (title + robots) per route touched, so a future accidental regression (e.g. someone removing `noindex` from a private page) fails a test immediately. Watch each new assertion fail against the current headless state first, implement, then green. Run `pnpm test` and `pnpm check`.

add_robots_txt_and_sitemap.s:
`static/robots.txt` currently exists but is a blanket allow-all with no `Sitemap:` line (`User-agent: *` / `Disallow:` — 3 lines total, already confirmed) — meaning crawlers currently waste budget crawling `/app/*` and `/api/*` (which just redirect to `/login` or 401 for any crawler with no session, zero indexable value) instead of being pointed at what's actually worth indexing. There's no sitemap or dedicated AI-crawler policy at all yet.

**1. Rewrite `static/robots.txt`** with an explicit policy: block the app shell and API (nothing crawlable there), explicitly and individually allow the major AI-answer-engine crawlers by name (the whole point of this plan per the user's own goal — "show up... in every AI chat" — several of these bots respect ONLY their own explicitly-named `User-agent` block and are more conservative about an unnamed wildcard than a human-search crawler would be, so don't rely on the wildcard rule alone to cover them), and point at the sitemap:
```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /app/
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /login
Allow: /

User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /

User-agent: anthropic-ai
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Perplexity-User
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /

User-agent: CCBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Bingbot
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://x2.apexlinks.workers.dev/sitemap.xml
```
(the `Sitemap:` line's domain must match whatever `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` actually resolves to per [[add_public_site_url_and_seo_head_component]] — since `static/robots.txt` is a static file, not a server route, it can't read `$env` at request time; keep this in sync manually whenever `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` changes, or convert it to a dynamic `+server.ts` route instead if it needs to stay perfectly in sync automatically — see the alternative below.)

**Alternative (recommended over the static file): make robots.txt dynamic too**, so it never drifts from `PUBLIC_SITE_URL`. Delete `static/robots.txt` and create `src/routes/robots.txt/+server.ts`:
```ts
import type { RequestHandler } from './$types';
import { env } from '$env/dynamic/private';

export const GET: RequestHandler = async () => {
	const body = `User-agent: *
Disallow: /app/
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /login
Allow: /

User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /

User-agent: anthropic-ai
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Perplexity-User
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /

User-agent: CCBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Bingbot
Allow: /

Sitemap: ${env.PUBLIC_SITE_URL}/sitemap.xml
`;
	return new Response(body, { headers: { 'content-type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' } });
};
```
Take this route over the static file — it's a few more lines but eliminates an entire class of "forgot to update robots.txt after changing domains" bugs, and this repo already has precedent for computed `+server.ts` responses with custom content-types (`src/routes/media/[...key]/+server.ts` for R2 streaming, per earlier research this session).

**2. Dynamic sitemap.** Create `src/routes/sitemap.xml/+server.ts` (new file) covering every indexable URL from the table in [[add_meta_titles_and_robots_per_route]] plus every public room and blog post:
```ts
import type { RequestHandler } from './$types';
import { env } from '$env/dynamic/private';
import { list_groups } from '$lib/server/group';
import { list_posts } from '$lib/server/blog';

function url(loc: string, changefreq: string, priority: string): string {
	return `<url><loc>${loc}</loc><changefreq>${changefreq}</changefreq><priority>${priority}</priority></url>`;
}

export const GET: RequestHandler = async () => {
	const base = env.PUBLIC_SITE_URL;
	const [rooms, posts] = await Promise.all([list_groups(env), list_posts(env)]);
	const entries = [
		url(base, 'daily', '1.0'),
		url(`${base}/app/rooms`, 'daily', '0.8'),
		url(`${base}/blog`, 'weekly', '0.7'),
		...rooms.map((g) => url(`${base}/app/rooms/${g.id}`, 'weekly', '0.5')),
		...posts.map((p) => url(`${base}/blog/${p.slug}`, 'monthly', '0.6'))
	];
	const body = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">\n${entries.join('\n')}\n</urlset>`;
	return new Response(body, { headers: { 'content-type': 'application/xml; charset=utf-8' } });
};
```
`list_groups(env)` with no `uid` already excludes paused/closed rooms per the other plan's `add_room_state_field` step (already executed by the time this runs) — the sitemap should never list a room its own search already hides. `list_posts`/the `blog.ts` module referenced here doesn't exist until [[add_blog_entity_and_seed_pipeline]] runs — if this step executes BEFORE that one, temporarily omit the `posts`/`list_posts` import and the `...posts.map(...)` line, and revisit this exact file once the blog step lands (call this out explicitly rather than silently shipping a broken import — check plan step order before implementing this one; steps are meant to leave the repo green independently, so if blog isn't built yet, ship the sitemap without blog entries now and extend it in [[add_blog_routes]] instead).

Room count could plausibly grow large — `list_groups`'s default `limit = 50` (per its signature in `group.ts`, already read in the other plan's research) caps this sitemap at 50 rooms today; if this ever matters at scale, paginate into a sitemap index (`sitemap-rooms-1.xml`, `sitemap-rooms-2.xml`, ...) — not needed yet, note it as the upgrade path rather than building it now (YAGNI at current scale, this is exactly a `ponytail:` scoped simplification: fixed 50-room single-file sitemap, paginate into a sitemap index if the room count ever exceeds it).

Test: create `src/routes/sitemap.xml/__tests__/server.test.ts` and `src/routes/robots.txt/__tests__/server.test.ts` (mirroring this codebase's established `vi.hoisted`/`vi.mock` style):
```ts
it('sitemap includes the home page, rooms list, and every returned room', async () => { ... });
it('sitemap response has an XML content-type', async () => { ... });
it('robots.txt disallows /app/ and /api/ but allows / generally', async () => { ... });
it('robots.txt explicitly allows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot', async () => { ... });
it('robots.txt Sitemap line uses PUBLIC_SITE_URL', async () => { ... });
```
Watch fail first, implement, then green. Run `pnpm test`.

add_alternative_landing_pages.s:
Dedicated, evergreen comparison landing pages — distinct from blog posts, and a real, well-established high-intent SEO/GEO pattern: "X alternative" search traffic (and the equivalent AI-answer-engine query, "what's a good alternative to X") converts far better against a page that IS the comparison (structured, scannable, directly answers the query) than against a blog post that merely discusses the topic. [[add_blog_entity_and_seed_pipeline]]'s `omegle-alternatives.md` and `x2-vs-omegle-vs-discord.md` posts already cover this topic in long form — these landing pages are a shorter, more structured, more directly-converting complement, not a replacement, and should cross-link with those posts rather than duplicate their content. Create `src/routes/alternatives/omegle/+page.svelte` (static content, no `+page.server.ts` load needed beyond `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` — reuse the same small server-load-for-site_url pattern established in every prior step of this plan): ```svelte
omegle alternative

looking for something like Omegle?

Omegle shut down in 2023. x2 keeps the part that made it worth using — talking to someone new, fast, no signup wall — and fixes the part that didn't: pure randomness. Search a room built around something you're actually into, or get matched by shared interest instead of pure chance.

search rooms — no account needed see the full comparison

no login to start

search and join without an account — one gets created for your device automatically the first time you actually chat.

interest-matched, not pure random

join a room about something specific, or get matched 1:1 weighted toward shared interests.

text, video, and groups

not just 1:1 — join a live group conversation, or call someone directly, all in one app.

``` Add a small `+page.server.ts` returning `{ site_url: env.PUBLIC_SITE_URL }`, same pattern as every prior step. Create `src/routes/alternatives/whatsapp/+page.svelte` following the identical structure, content adapted from `whatsapp-alternatives.md`'s honest framing (the "meet new people vs. message existing contacts" split) — title `"a WhatsApp alternative for meeting new people"`, cross-linking to `/blog/whatsapp-alternatives`. Both pages get added to `src/routes/sitemap.xml/+server.ts`'s static `entries` array (alongside `/`, `/app/rooms`, `/blog`) and cross-linked FROM their corresponding blog posts — edit `content/blog/omegle-alternatives.md`'s closing CTA line and `x2-vs-omegle-vs-discord.md`'s closing line to link to `/alternatives/omegle` instead of the bare `/` home link they currently end on, and `whatsapp-alternatives.md`'s closing line to `/alternatives/whatsapp` — small, surgical edits to already-written files, not a rewrite of their content. Test: create component tests for both new pages asserting the title/description/CTA hrefs, and extend `sitemap.xml`'s test with the two new static entries. Watch fail first, implement, then green. Run `pnpm test` and `pnpm check`.

add_footer_and_internal_linking.s:
No footer exists anywhere in the app today (confirmed — `src/routes/+layout.svelte`, full file already read multiple times this session, has a `
` and a mobile bottom nav but no `
`). Internal linking is a real, well-established ranking factor (it's how crawlers discover pages and how link equity flows from high-authority pages like the home page to newer ones like blog posts) and right now the only paths into `/blog` or `/alternatives/*` are direct URL knowledge — nothing on the home page or anywhere else in the app links to them at all once this plan's other steps have built them. Add a footer to `src/routes/+layout.svelte`, rendered on every page (unlike the header/bottom-nav, which are gated behind `{#if data.user}` — a footer with links to public content should appear for logged-out visitors too, arguably especially for them, since that's exactly who's arriving from search/AI-answer-engine traffic and needs a path to the rest of the site). Insert after `
` closes (after line 96, before the `{#if data.user}` block that starts the mobile nav): ```svelte
rooms blog omegle alternative whatsapp alternative

© {new Date().getFullYear()} x2

``` Four links, not a sprawling sitemap-in-a-footer — this repo's product surface is genuinely small (rooms, blog, two alternative pages) and a footer padded with placeholder links (About, Careers, Press) that go nowhere would be worse for both users and crawlers than an honest, short one; add more links here only when there's an actual page for them to point to, not preemptively. Cross-link between blog posts themselves — right now each of the 9 posts only links back to `/` (or, after [[add_alternative_landing_pages]], the two `/alternatives/*` pages) and never to each other, missing an easy internal-linking win between clearly related posts (e.g. `random-chat-apps-compared.md` and `random-video-chat-safety.md` cover adjacent territory and should reference each other). Add one short "related" link at the end of each post's body, before its closing CTA line, pointing to the single most topically-related other post: - `omegle-alternatives.md` → link to `x2-vs-omegle-vs-discord` - `whatsapp-alternatives.md` → link to `make-new-friends-online` - `make-new-friends-online.md` → link to `group-chat-guide` - `no-login-chat-apps.md` → link to `omegle-alternatives` - `random-chat-apps-compared.md` → link to `random-video-chat-safety` - `find-chat-groups.md` → link to `group-chat-guide` - `random-video-chat-safety.md` → link to `random-chat-apps-compared` - `x2-vs-omegle-vs-discord.md` → link to `omegle-alternatives` - `group-chat-guide.md` → link to `find-chat-groups` Each as one added sentence/link (e.g. in `random-chat-apps-compared.md`, before the closing `---` CTA: `Curious specifically about the safety side of random video chat? [Read the full breakdown](/blog/random-video-chat-safety).`) — small, surgical edits to the already-written files, not rewrites. Test: extend `src/routes/__tests__/layout.svelte.test.ts` with: the footer renders on every page regardless of `data.user`, and contains links to `/app/rooms`, `/blog`, `/alternatives/omegle`, `/alternatives/whatsapp`. Add a lightweight content-integrity test, `content/blog/__tests__/cross-links.test.ts` (or colocated per wherever this repo's non-route content tests conventionally live), asserting every post file contains at least one `](/blog/` internal link to another post, so a future edit that accidentally strips these is caught: ```ts import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'; import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs'; import { join } from 'node:path'; it('every blog post links to at least one other blog post', () => { const dir = join(process.cwd(), 'content/blog'); for (const file of readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.md'))) { const body = readFileSync(join(dir, file), 'utf-8'); expect(body).toMatch(/\]\(\/blog\//); } }); ``` Watch both fail first (no footer, no cross-links yet), implement, then green. Run `pnpm test` and `pnpm check`.
